text.p: Iraq said on Thursday "American aggression" against it was continuing and vowed to resist it.
Iraqi television said President Saddam Hussein chaired a joint meeting of the Revolutionary Command Council and the regional command of the ruling Baath party.

It quoted a spokesman for the council as saying after the meeting that Baghdad would consider the U.S. military mission against Iraq ended only when U.S. planes stopped violating Iraq's airspace and threatening its sovereignty.

"We consider that the American aggression along with those taking part in it is continuing and we shall go on resisting it on the basis of the legitimacy of self-defence and national sovereignty," it quoted the spokesman as saying.

The United States fired cruise missiles against air defence targets in southern Iraq on Tuesday and Wednesday after the Iraqi military helped a Kurdish faction seize the northern city of Arbil from a rival group on Saturday.
U.S. President Bill Clinton said on Wednesday the U.S. mission in Iraq "has been achieved" by the missile attacks and Iraq has withdrawn its forces from the Kurdish area at least for the time being.
The Iraqi spokesman said of the Clinton remarks: "By announcing that, the Americans are trying to mislead world public opinion, as if their aggression on Iraq has ended while it is continuing."

The United States and Britain this week declared an extension of the no-fly zone they have been enforcing along with France in southern Iraq since 1992, taking its northern limit to the 33rd parallel, 50 km (30 miles) south of Baghdad.
France said on Thursday its planes would continue patrolling southern Iraqi skies but would not cross the 32nd parallel, the northern limit of the old zone.
All three countries continue to enforce an air exclusion zone in northern Iraq they declared shortly after in the 1991 Gulf War.
The television said Saddam also met Defence Minister General Sultan Hashim Ahmed and commanders of the Iraqi Republican Guard and air defence command. It gave no details.
